deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (IV) 'ind-espaces modérés' of Grothendieck's axiomatic tame-topology notes. A 'tame structure' is given axiomatically: a base set R (think the reals), tame parts of the R^n, and axioms M1–M9. The previous page defines a strict ind-tame space as a set E with a family M_E of subsets (the tame parts). M_E is stable under finite unions and covers E. Each member carries a tame structure, these structures induce one another, and A in M_E, B in M_A implies B in M_E. Under axiom M8 (R is the union of its tame parts), R and every R^I become ind-tame spaces canonically. The category of ind-tame spaces has finite limits and, if R_0 is non-empty, finite sums, all compatible with the forgetful functor X -> |X|.

This page continues as follows.

(1) Definition. Let 𝔛 be an ind-tame space. A subset Y of 𝔛 is 'locally tame' if A ∩ Y is in M_𝔛 for every A in M_𝔛. This is the analogue of a closed subset of a compactly generated space, or of an admissible (locally definable) subset of a locally semialgebraic or definable space.

(2) Stability.
- Locally tame subsets are stable under finite intersections, including the empty intersection, so 𝔛 itself is locally tame.
- They are stable under inverse images by morphisms of ind-tame spaces.

(3) Consistency check. The earlier notion of a tame map from a tame space X to R^I is a special case of a morphism of ind-tame spaces. This holds once M8 is satisfied, so that X and R^I become ind-tame spaces.

(4) Colimits. Assuming M6 and M7, the category of ind-tame spaces has two kinds of colimit, both compatible with the forgetful functor X -> |X|:
- quotients 𝔛/𝔜 (collapsing 𝔜) when 𝔜 is a locally tame subset;
- amalgamated sums 𝔛_1 ⊔_ℨ 𝔛_2 along 'locally tame immersions' ℨ -> 𝔛_i. These are maps that identify ℨ with locally tame parts Z_i ⊂ X_i (continued on p.16).

The next page warns that subobjects (monomorphisms) in Esp_M need not correspond to locally tame parts. It then passes to relations with topology: axiom M9 says tame parts of R^n are compact, so the forgetful functor factors through topological spaces.

Purpose: build a category of tame spaces closed under the gluing operations of homotopy theory (cell attachment, collapsing). That category would be a 'tame' substitute for CW complexes or compactly generated spaces. This is the programme later announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: Stability under inverse image tacitly needs two things for a morphism f: 𝔛' -> 𝔛. First, each tame part A' of 𝔛' must map into some tame part A of 𝔛. Second, inverse images of tame parts by tame maps must be tame (presumably among M1–M7). The page does not state these.

No proof or verification is given that the quotients and pushouts exist. Only the assumptions M6, M7 are cited, so this remains a claim. It is plausible: the analogous statements for weakly semialgebraic spaces need a closedness/properness-type hypothesis, which 'locally tame' plays here.

The text gives no precise definition of 'immersion loc. modérée' beyond 'corresponding to a locally tame part'. The next page itself flags that subobjects need not be locally tame parts, i.e. monomorphisms are not the same as embeddings.

ideas.what: Ind-tame spaces: a set exhausted by a filtering family of tame subsets, with compatible tame structures
ideas.modern_name: locally definable / weakly definable spaces; ind-definable sets; locally semialgebraic and weakly semialgebraic spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985); Knebusch (weakly semialgebraic spaces, 1989); Piękosz and Edmundo et al. in the o-minimal setting (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5; the ind-construction itself is unsure/not published

ideas.what: Locally tame subset: Y with A∩Y tame for every tame A; stable under finite intersections and inverse images
ideas.modern_name: admissible / locally definable subset (closed in the weak topology); analogue of k-closed sets in compactly generated spaces

ideas.what: Existence of quotients X/Y by locally tame Y and pushouts along locally tame immersions, commuting with the underlying-set functor
ideas.modern_name: gluing and cell attachment in weakly semialgebraic / weakly definable spaces; definable quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knebusch (Weakly semialgebraic spaces, LNM 1367, 1989); van den Dries (Tame topology, 1998, definable quotients); Piękosz

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'ind-espaces modérés', with locally tame parts and gluings along them, anticipate the category of locally/weakly semialgebraic spaces (Delfs–Knebusch 1985, Knebusch 1989) and the later o-minimal 'weakly definable spaces'. Those are built precisely to allow CW-type gluings. The historical precedence (1970s) and the axiomatic, structure-independent setting do not seem to be recorded in that literature.
missed.quote: Une partie de 𝔛 est dite loc. modérée si ∀A∈M_𝔛, on a A∩Y∈M_𝔛 ... il existe ... des quotients 𝔛/𝔜 ... si 𝔜 est partie localt modérée, et des 𝔛_1 ⊔_ℨ 𝔛_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical credit and context point for the 'tame topology' programme. It shows Grothendieck already intended a cocomplete-enough category of tame spaces suitable for homotopy theory, which is relevant to current work on o-minimal homotopy theory and condensed/definable approaches.

missed.claim: The precise colimit-closure properties (which colimits exist, and the role of axioms M6, M7) are asserted but not proved. The mismatch between monomorphisms and locally tame parts is flagged but left open.
missed.quote: Moyennant M6, M7, il existe ... des quotients
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small axiomatic question: which minimal axioms on an abstract tame structure guarantee these gluings. It is answered piecemeal for semialgebraic and o-minimal cases but not in Grothendieck's axiomatic generality.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas are sketchy and essentially those later developed independently, as locally/weakly semialgebraic and definable spaces. What is mildly notable is the early date and the abstract axiomatic framing of ind-tame spaces with gluings, which is not documented in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'quand M_f est satisfait dans X et R^I considérés comme des espaces ind-modérés' should read approximately 'quand M8 est satisfait (X et R^I deviennent des espaces ind-modérés)'. This refers to axiom M8 of the previous page.
'il existe [-pour-] des Esp_{M_i} ... 𝔛/𝔜 ...' should read approximately 'il existe dans Esp_{Mi} [ind-modérés] des quotients 𝔛/𝔜 (commutant au foncteur X ↦ |X|)'.
'et de =' is likely 'et des' (introducing the amalgamated sums 𝔛_1 ⊔_ℨ 𝔛_2).
Line 3: 'on a A∩Y∈M_𝔛' — Grothendieck first wrote 𝔛 and then corrected it; the subset is Y.
